Abstract#1: Jill Godmilow discusses her film, The Popovich Brothers of South Chicago (1977). In this recording, the audience and panel members discuss how marginalized communities are represented in society and maintain their sense of culture when faced with matters of representation and assimilation. Godmilow participates in a panel with University of Colorado Regent Dr. Geraldine Bean; Chris Gutierrez, director of University Minority Programs; and, Norbert Hill, director of the American Indian Educational Opportunity Program (AIEOP), sharing personal experiences and general cultural perceptions.

Don Yannacito introduces Godmilow for a Q&A session. 00:00:49 Godmilow discusses film distribution, market, the documentary format, and the Serbian community's role in these matters regarding the film, The Popvich Brothers of South Chicago (1977). She mentions the role of music in the culture. 00:05:22 Godmilow provides background into how she became involved with the film, mentioning the Balkan Art Center in New York. Godmilow comments on how she hopes the film will be used in an academic setting and explains influences on her work, including the films of Les Blank. 00:07:30 Godmilow discusses filmmaking process and how the limitations of the documentary filmmaking process affected the end result. She addresses the death of the youngest Popovich brother early on in the production and how the film was funded. 00:12:00 Godmilow expounds on her relationship with the Popovich brothers, how the different generations of the community altered the filmmaking process, and the role of being personal, both as a filmmaker and subject. 00:16:56 Don Yannacito introduces the second part of the program: a panel discussion with Godmilow, Dr. Geraldine Bean, Chris Gutierrez, and Norbert Hill. 00:19:00 The panel compares the cultures of the ethnic minorities in the film to those in Colorado. The role of music is emphasized, as well as a sense of community. Issues of assimilation are brought into question, specifically regarding education, professionalism, identity, and discrimination. 00:26:00 The panel discussion shifts to the role of gender in culture, specifically men in Serbia. Abstract#1: As an event in the First Person Cinema series at the University of Colorado Boulder, video artist Vanalyne Green screens and discusses her works, Trick or Drink (1984) and A Spy in the House That Ruth Built (1990).
